chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Repertoire with Al Dennie and checking details of the early years
summary: Asked what he played, he says stock arrangements and tunes like Honeysuckle Rose, playing chords by ear; the Dances check spellings and the length of his stays.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: : JAY, just before you get that far, now seriously, I mean, you weren't playing piano everyday at home or anywhere.
No.
: Well, I mean, exactly what kind of a repertoire did you have when you sat down with Al Denny's band? What were they playing? Stock arrangements?
They were playing stocks.
: On regular tunes?
On tunes.
: 'Honeysuckle Rose,' stuff like that?
Uh-huh, whatever, you know, 'Kansas City Kitty.' Let me see, what were some of these other tunes? Tunes like 'Judy,' you know --
(Inaudible).
Yeah, like that.
: And in every case, you just played the chords.
Just went right along with them, whichever way they went, you know?
: And the tunes, you could retain them.
I could retain them. Well, you know, you happen to hear something new to retain.
: Yeah.
So it's no trouble. You set it in
there one time and it's there, you know?
(Laughter.)
Well, listen, so you'd get a chance to go for yourself, what would you do? Just sort of play that melody?
Oh, you mean when they'd tell me to play the solo?
Yes.

Oh, yes. I played the melody like I wanted to play it. I just played the way that I wanted to play it and then when the band came back in and I could go on back with the "boom-chink, boom-chink, boom-chink," which was the beginning of the "complimenting the blues."
(Laughter.)
But it says here, Jay, that you were with that band for four months. Is that right? With Al Denny?
How's that?
You were with Al Denny -- was it Dennis or Denny?
D-e-n-n-i-e, Dennie.
D-e-n-n- --
i-e.
i-e.
Uh-huh.
They've got Dennis here.
Yeah, it was Dennie. Yeah, he was -- a lot of times, they make mistake on the --
Yeah. But when you (unintelligible) spent two months as Fisk. Had you been at Fisk?
We didn't spent two months, we spent about a month there, about a month.
Yeah.
Yeah, it was about a month there, see, because we didn't have -- we just didn't have enough money to carry us.
Who was it though you told me you used to raid the landlady's refrigerator?
Oh, that was later on when I was in junior college, when I used to raid the landlady's frigidaire.
(Laughter.)
